conventions: Comment-only change: no executable line, signature, type, name, import or declaration order changes in any unit. Only TSDoc comment blocks are added or replaced.
The Apache 2.0 license header stays byte-identical at the top of every edited file, original year included. Never bump a year.
Prettier 2 via @backstage/cli/config/prettier: 80-column print width, single quotes, trailing commas. Let the check's fix form reformat rather than hand-wrapping.
TSDoc prose is third-person declarative ('Checks that...', 'Sets...', 'Narrows...'); the first sentence is short and indexable; never open with 'This function' or an imperative.
Tag order inside every block: description, then @remarks, then the release tag, then @param, @returns, @throws.
Every @param uses the form '@param name - description'; the hyphen is required (STYLE.md:234) or API Extractor warns.
{@link Symbol} for in-package cross-references; '@see https://...' with a bare URL for external specs, matching CommonValidatorFunctions.
@remarks only where the text runs longer than two lines; a short block is one paragraph with no @remarks.
Documented members of a type, interface or class carry no release tag of their own; only the enclosing declaration does, and its existing tag is reused verbatim.
No test file is touched and no test is added. The package's existing 64 suites / 893 tests are the regression check.
packages/catalog-model/report.api.md and report-alpha.api.md are generated by API Extractor and are never hand-edited; no unit writes them.

decisions.topic: Shape of an added member comment (interface member, class method, static)
decisions.choice: A multi-line block comment on its own lines directly above the member, as in src/entity/Entity.ts: '/**', ' * text', ' */'.
decisions.reason: The compact form is used in this package only for inline nested members such as the parseEntityRef context object; every documented interface member and class member uses the multi-line block.

decisions.topic: Release tag on each added block
decisions.choice: Reuse the tag packages/catalog-model/report.api.md already shows for the enclosing declaration; added member blocks carry no tag at all.
decisions.reason: --validate-release-tags is active in build:api-reports, so a wrong or duplicated tag turns today's silent omission into a hard build failure.

decisions.topic: Editing the existing '/** @public */' blocks in src/entity/conditions.ts
decisions.choice: Replace the whole three-line comment block per function with a new block holding description, then @public, then @param entity.
rejected: Inserting description lines before the ' * @public' line and a @param line after it
decisions.reason: One replace site per function keeps tag order correct in one edit and leaves no chance of a stray second comment opener.

decisions.topic: Tag set on the five enforce methods
decisions.choice: Description, '@param entity - ...', '@returns ...', and '@throws ...' only on the methods whose own body throws (FieldFormatEntityPolicy, NoForeignRootFieldsEntityPolicy, SchemaValidEntityPolicy).
decisions.reason: Mirrors the EntityPolicy.enforce block in src/entity/policies/types.ts while staying accurate: DefaultNamespaceEntityPolicy.enforce and GroupDefaultParentEntityPolicy.enforce never throw (GroupDefaultParentEntityPolicy throws from its constructor only).

decisions.topic: Wording for the apiVersion and kind members of the eight kind interfaces
decisions.choice: State that the member narrows the inherited Entity field to the literal value(s) this kind accepts, and name those literals.
rejected: Describing apiVersion as a version-negotiation or migration mechanism
decisions.reason: Both members are literal discriminators in the source; the code expresses nothing beyond the accepted literals and must not be given invented semantics.

decisions.choice: State the literal rule only: a string of 1 to 63 characters that begins and ends with [A-Za-z0-9] and may contain [-_.] in between. No @see.
rejected: Calling it a DNS subdomain name and linking the Kubernetes object-names document
decisions.reason: The regex permits uppercase letters, underscores and dots, so it is neither the DNS subdomain nor the DNS label rule the names document describes; no single Kubernetes document matches it, and a wrong @see is worse than none.

decisions.choice: Describe the rule the delegate actually enforces and cross-reference it with {@link CommonValidatorFunctions.isValidDnsLabel} / {@link CommonValidatorFunctions.isValidDnsSubdomain} / {@link KubernetesValidatorFunctions.isValidObjectName}.
rejected: Describing the rule from the member name
Only saying that the call is delegated
decisions.reason: isValidNamespace, isValidLabelKey, isValidAnnotationKey, isValidLabelValue and isValidApiVersion all delegate; a reader needs the enforced rule, and the link gives the exact predicate.

decisions.topic: Where the two API reports come from
decisions.choice: No unit edits packages/catalog-model/report.api.md or report-alpha.api.md; they are regenerated by the run's acceptance check outside the spec.
rejected: A unit that hand-edits the reports
A tooling unit that runs yarn build:api-reports
decisions.reason: The files carry API Extractor's do-not-edit banner, and a docs job may hold no tooling unit; regeneration is the person's acceptance step.

decisions.topic: Changeset file name and bump level
decisions.choice: A new .changeset/plain-models-explain.md naming '@backstage/catalog-model' at patch, one adopter-facing sentence, no internal symbol names.
rejected: Reusing one of the 38 pending changesets
decisions.reason: Documentation-only on a published package at 1.10.2 is a patch; no pending changeset names this package; project instructions forbid the CLI and require editing .changeset files directly.

units.behaviour: Adds a TSDoc block above each of the eight statics of KubernetesValidatorFunctions, stating the rule each one actually enforces, clearing eight (undocumented) markers.
rules: 1. Add exactly eight blocks, one per site, each a multi-line block directly above the static it documents.

2. Each block is: a one-sentence description, then '@param value - The value to check', then '@see <url>' only where the site's rule names one. No release tag on any block: the class's own block with its @public and its three @see lines stays byte-identical.
3. The first sentence opens with 'Checks that the value is' or 'Checks that the value matches', as every static of CommonValidatorFunctions does.

4. State the rule the implementation enforces, never the one the member name suggests. Where the implementation delegates, describe the delegate's rule and cross-reference the delegate with {@link ...}.
5. A non-string input is rejected by every one of these, so no block claims a coercion or a non-string case.
6. Change no expression, no regex, no member order and no import.
7. Do not edit packages/catalog-model/report.api.md or report-alpha.api.md. They carry API Extractor's do-not-edit banner and are regenerated by yarn build:api-reports outside this change.

sites.rule: Rule enforced: either '<suffix>' alone or '<prefix>/<suffix>'; the prefix must be a valid DNS subdomain ({@link CommonValidatorFunctions.isValidDnsSubdomain}) and the suffix 1 to 63 characters of [a-zA-Z0-9] only. More than one slash is rejected. @see https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/overview/working-with-objects/names/
Rule enforced inline: a string of 1 to 63 characters that starts with a letter and continues with letters and digits only. No @see: no Kubernetes document states this rule.

Rule enforced inline: a string of 1 to 63 characters that begins and ends with [A-Za-z0-9] and may contain dashes, underscores and dots in between. State that uppercase letters are accepted. No @see: this is neither the DNS subdomain nor the DNS label rule, so no Kubernetes document matches it.

Rule enforced by delegation to {@link CommonValidatorFunctions.isValidDnsLabel}: a valid DNS label — 1 to 63 lowercase alphanumeric characters in dash-separated groups. @see https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc1123

Rule enforced: either '<name>' alone or '<prefix>/<name>'; the prefix must be a valid DNS subdomain ({@link CommonValidatorFunctions.isValidDnsSubdomain}) and the name must satisfy {@link KubernetesValidatorFunctions.isValidObjectName}. @see https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/overview/working-with-objects/labels/#syntax-and-character-set

Rule enforced: the empty string, or a value that satisfies {@link KubernetesValidatorFunctions.isValidObjectName}. The empty string being allowed is the one difference from the object-name rule and must be stated. @see https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/overview/working-with-objects/labels/#syntax-and-character-set

Rule enforced: the same prefix-and-or-name rule as {@link KubernetesValidatorFunctions.isValidLabelKey} — either '<name>' alone or '<prefix>/<name>', the prefix a valid DNS subdomain and the name a valid object name. @see https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/overview/working-with-objects/annotations/#syntax-and-character-set

Rule enforced inline: any string at all, the empty string included. No length limit and no character restriction; say so plainly rather than implying a format. @see https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/overview/working-with-objects/annotations/#syntax-and-character-set

units.behaviour: Replaces the bare '/** @public */' block above each of the eight entity type guards with a documented block, clearing eight (undocumented) markers.
rules: 1. Each site replaces a whole three-line comment block with a new block holding, in this order: a one-line description, a blank comment line, ' * @public', then '@param entity - The entity to check'.
2. The '@public' tag is reused exactly; no tag is added, removed or changed.

3. Each description states both facts that hold of the implementation: the check compares entity.kind without regard to case, and the function is a type guard that narrows the entity to the named kind's interface. Name the interface with {@link ...} using the alias the function's signature returns.
4. Mention the kind literal the implementation compares against ('API', 'Component', 'Domain', 'Group', 'Location', 'Resource', 'System', 'User' respectively).
5. No @returns: the narrowing is the return value and stating it twice adds nothing.
6. Keep the file's existing shape of no blank line between one function's closing brace and the next function's comment block.
7. Change no function body, no signature, no import and no declaration order.

units.behaviour: Adds a TSDoc block above FieldFormatEntityPolicy.enforce describing which fields it validates and its throw behaviour, clearing one (undocumented) marker.
rules: 1. One multi-line block directly above the method, holding a description, then @remarks listing the fields checked, then '@param entity - The entity to apply the policy to', '@returns ...' and '@throws ...'.
2. No release tag: the class's own block with its @public and @remarks stays byte-identical.

3. The @remarks names the fields the body actually checks: apiVersion and kind are required; metadata.name is required; metadata.namespace is checked only when present; every label key and value, every annotation key and value, and every tag are checked; for each entry of metadata.links the url is required and the title and icon are checked only when present.
4. '@returns' states that the entity is returned unchanged — this policy validates and never mutates.
5. '@throws' states that an Error is thrown on the first failure, and that its message names the failing field and, where the validator is a known one, the expected format.
6. State that a required field holding undefined or null fails as a missing value.
7. Do not list the validator function names: the set is configurable through the constructor's Validators argument, so name the fields, not the predicates.
8. Change no expression, no import and no member order.

units.behaviour: Adds the run's changeset, naming @backstage/catalog-model at patch with an adopter-facing description of the added API documentation.
rules: 1. The file is exactly a YAML front matter block delimited by '---' lines holding the single line "'@backstage/catalog-model': patch", a blank line, then one paragraph of prose. Nothing else.
2. The package name is single-quoted, matching every other changeset in .changeset/.
3. The bump is patch. Never minor and never major: no API surface changes.

4. The prose is one or two sentences in plain language, present tense, written for adopters: the catalog entity kinds, the entity type guards, the Kubernetes-compatible validators and the entity policies now carry API documentation describing what each accepts and enforces.
5. Name no internal symbol, no file, no class and no function. Refer to the surfaces by what an adopter calls them.
6. Say that this is a documentation change with no behaviour change.
7. No markdown heading, no list, no code fence, no link.
8. Add no license header: changesets are markdown, not source.

style_from.reason: The repo's changeset shape: single-quoted package name and a patch bump in front matter, then one adopter-facing paragraph with no headings.
